blurb: The logarithm from ∫dt/t to the complex plane: rigorous foundations, series, entropy, primes and discrete logs.

pics.alt: Plot of the ratios π(x)/(x/ln x) and π(x)/Li(x) against x on a logarithmic axis from 1 to 10^24
pics.caption: The prime number theorem in pictures: both π(x)/(x/ln x) and π(x)/∫₂ˣ dt/ln t tend to 1, but the logarithmic-integral approximation converges far faster.
pics.title: Prime number theorem ratio convergence.svg

pics.alt: Helicoidal Riemann surface of the complex logarithm, coloured by argument
pics.caption: The Riemann surface of log z: the imaginary part arg z rises by 2π each time z circles the origin, so the sheets stack into an infinite helicoid over the punctured plane.
pics.title: Riemann surface log.svg
